dossier.architecture: Under-bumper collector, pivoted launcher and reversible backpack amp/trap route.

subsystems.drivetrain: Swerve; centering wedges extend over module areas.
subsystems.intake: Silicone-wrapped rollers and low-friction wedges center notes.
subsystems.transfer: Two-roller feeder can reverse into the backpack path.
subsystems.scoring: Sector-gear pivot with steel reinforcement; asymmetrical wheel arrangement adds spin.
subsystems.endgame: Tilted hook elevator lifts robot; backpack raises and reverses note into trap.
subsystems.controls: Four Limelights localize; absolute pivot sensing controls shot angle.

versions: Powered/pliant cap geometry evolved to handle both amp and trap angles; Open Alliance thread supplies the longer development history.
dossier.analysis: This is an especially useful source for how packaging, service access and control states develop together. The U-turn note path solves two destinations but must tolerate different release angles.
limits: Intermediate undocumented changes are not inferred; specifications and plans retain their source context.

context_documents.title: 2024-3847 · Centering, spin and reverse transfer share one constrained path
context_documents.body:
# 2024-3847: Centering, spin and reverse transfer share one constrained path

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

Silicone-wrapped collector rollers, Teflon-covered wedges and additional module guides center the note. A two-roller feeder can reverse it into the backpack amp/trap path. Asymmetric black-wheel placement produces spin, while the main scoring pivot uses sector gearing with reinforcement.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly identifies the full-width intake with driver margin and the contact materials with centering. The backpack receives the note through a reversed feed sequence.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Forward and reverse transport must both control a flexible ring. A low-friction wedge is useful for centering but may provide little retention while the robot reverses direction or lifts the note. The launcher’s intended asymmetry also depends on repeatable centering. A shared path saves hardware only if direction changes do not create a high jam or alignment burden.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Test reversed handoffs after aggressive pickup, measure note pose before each route, and verify chain clearance through the climb/backpack sequence.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.
